semanticRail.law: TypeScript is the authority for strict Vue/Svelte projection typing: hover types, diagnostics, project checks, completion types. Provider modes select which TypeScript engine answers; nothing else does. This restates the STP0 type-authority law at the consumer boundary.

inspectionRail.law: Native flow facts, native-checker observations, compiler analyses and component-meta are separately labelled inspection answers. They may describe the same source file but are labelled, carry their own provenance, and never substitute a semantic-rail answer.
inspectionRail.labellingEvidence: hover provenance display (verter.hover.provenance setting; hover init-option key) is the existing labelling edge this generalizes

comparisonRail.law: Comparing rails (native inspection vs TypeScript) is an explicitly selected operation per request, in the lineage of the STP1 verify-node engine comparisons. Silent substitution, or a comparison offered as the default answer to a semantic question, is forbidden.

discriminators.scenario: In one source file, native flow-return facts (inspection rail) and TypeScript hover/diagnostics (semantic rail) stay separately queryable, separately labelled, and never merge into one answer or one authority.

forbidden: silent comparison as the default answer
merging the two authorities into one engine or one answer channel
